reference: The runnable contracts use Bash's type/help builtins and the checked-in pkill registration/help contract in pkill.c, cross-checked with sol-pkill.md and sol-pgrep.md. No process-selection or signal-delivery result is claimed as GNU parity.
coverage: Bash reports pkill as a builtin.
Registered help exposes the pkill synopsis, POSIX ERE behavior, and self-exclusion statement.
Registered help exposes full-command matching, exact matching, count, newest/oldest, and selectors.
Registered help exposes documented result statuses.
Metadata results are not operation coverage; deferred operations are not passes.
exclusions: No pkill operation is executed because it can send process signals.
Signal delivery, procfs selection, matching, delivery failures, and process-age selection remain deferred pending a disposable VM or fail-closed syscall mock.
GNU pkill operation parity is not claimed; metadata contract checks are not operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Bash's type -t contract should identify the pinned pkill loadable as a builtin without invoking it.
The registered Bash help metadata should expose the documented signal/pattern synopsis, POSIX ERE contract, and self-exclusion behavior.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pkill)
if [[ $doc == *"[-SIGNAL] [-cfx] [-n|-o] [SELECTORS] [PATTERN]"* && $doc == *"[-SIGNAL] [-cf] -u USER"* && $doc == *"PATTERN is a POSIX extended regular expression."* && $doc == *"Self is never signalled."* ]]; then
  printf 'pkill help synopsis and matching contract present\n'
else
  exit 1
fi
cases.stdout: pkill help synopsis and matching contract present

cases.purpose: The registered help metadata should describe full-command matching, exact matching, count output, and newest/oldest selection.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pkill)
if [[ $doc == *"full command line"* && $doc == *"-c, --count"* && $doc == *"-x, --exact"* && $doc == *"-n, --newest"* && $doc == *"-o, --oldest"* ]]; then
  printf 'pkill matching options documented\n'
else
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: The registered help metadata should list supported identity/process selectors and the documented success, no-match, usage, and fatal status meanings.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pkill)
if [[ $doc == *"-u USER"* && $doc == *"-U USER"* && $doc == *"-G GROUP"* && $doc == *"-P PID"* && $doc == *"-g PGRP"* && $doc == *"-s SID"* && $doc == *"Returns 0 if any request succeeded, 1 if none, 2 on usage error, 3 on fatal."* ]]; then
  printf 'pkill selectors and status contract documented\n'
else
  exit 1
fi
cases.stdout: pkill selectors and status contract documented

cases.purpose: Verify default TERM reaches only selected private fixture processes and never the invoking shell.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with uniquely named, test-owned child processes, parent-PID restriction, and signal acknowledgements, or a reviewed fail-closed procfs/kill syscall mock that records every target. This environment's safety rules prohibit invoking pkill operations.

cases.purpose: Verify named and numeric signal parsing, signal zero, -c output, and success/no-match statuses against controlled delivery results.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a private owned-process set or a fail-closed kill interceptor that records signal numbers and injects successes and failures; no real signal operation is permitted in this suite.

cases.purpose: Verify POSIX ERE matching, -f/-x command-line behavior, and combined UID/parent selectors against a known process set.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with isolated process fixtures or a synthetic procfs adapter plus a fail-closed kill mock and independent PID-set arithmetic. Running pkill against a live process table is prohibited here.

cases.purpose: Verify -n/-o select the expected single process, including equal-start-time PID tie breaking.
cases.reason: Requires deterministic synthetic proc stat records and a kill syscall mock that captures the single chosen PID; live process ages are not a safe deterministic oracle.

cases.purpose: Verify invalid regexes/options produce usage status without any signal request, and that ESRCH/EPERM failures affect diagnostics, count, and final status as documented.
cases.reason: Requires an isolated synthetic proc tree and fail-closed kill mock with injected errno results and an assertion that invalid input makes zero delivery calls. Invoking operation cases is outside the permitted safety scope.
